title: How jelly works
about: One daemon, one store, one lock. Everything that changes a jelly takes the same road.

nodes.label: The agent
nodes.what: Any agent with a shell. It only ever talks to jelly through the CLI.

nodes.label: The person
nodes.what: Uses jellies in a browser: clicks, answers, comments.

nodes.label: The jelly CLI
nodes.what: One binary. Every command but `serve` is an HTTP request to the daemon (ureq), and most print one line.
files: src/main.rs: run, report, placement, inbox, detect_project

touched.note: placement turns `anchor` into the sentence the agent reads.

nodes.label: runtime.js
nodes.what: `window.jelly` in every view: call, onState, comments, question cards, and the text snapshot for `jelly see`.
files: assets/runtime.js: jelly.call, apply, drawAttention, placeAfter, deadAnchors, postSnapshot
nodes.risk: One WebSocket per page. An EventSource per view would hit the browser's six-per-host limit.

nodes.label: A jelly's view
nodes.what: Any HTML the agent wrote, served at /j/<id>/ with the runtime injected first in <head>.
nodes.risk: Keep the trailing slash in /j/<id>/: relative `assets/<file>` paths depend on it.

nodes.label: The jelly page
nodes.what: The internal jelly, id `surface`, that lays out the others. Each jelly on it is an iframe of /j/<id>/.
nodes.risk: It is a jelly too: its own verb calls are events like any other.

nodes.label: Screens
nodes.what: What a browser last showed of each jelly, as text, with page errors and dead anchors. Memory only.
nodes.risk: Gone on restart, and the last poster wins: an open view and a headless render both write here.

nodes.label: see and the anchor check
nodes.what: Renders a jelly in headless Chrome and reads back what the page says is on screen. `jelly see` prints it; an ask with --at uses it to check its anchor.
files: src/server.rs: see, render, anchor_place, RENDER_LIMIT, ANCHOR_CHECK
nodes.risk: Headless Chrome often posts its snapshot and then does not exit. anchor_place answers when the snapshot is in; see still waits for the browser (issue #6).

touched.note: anchor_place is new; render takes a time limit.

nodes.label: Routes
nodes.what: The axum router: one handler per thing you can do to a jelly. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, with no login.
files: src/server.rs: serve, call, set_state, reshape, attend, comment
nodes.risk: Anything that can reach the port can run verbs.

touched.note: attend checks the anchor after the item is made, and adds `anchor` to its reply.

nodes.label: App::change
nodes.what: Every write goes through here: take the store lock, run one store change, broadcast its event.
nodes.risk: The lock is what makes verbs run one at a time. Do not write state around it.

nodes.label: Broadcast channel
nodes.what: A tokio broadcast channel of events, 1024 deep. Browsers hear it over the WebSocket; `jelly wait` and `jelly events` hear it over /api/events.
nodes.risk: A listener that falls behind is told to resync (the page reloads).

nodes.label: WebSocket
nodes.what: /api/ws: one task per open page forwards every event as JSON.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md tokens
nodes.what: A project's DESIGN.md front matter, flattened into CSS variables at /p/<project>/design.css.

nodes.label: Store
nodes.what: Every jelly in memory, behind one Mutex. Each change bumps the version, saves the jelly and returns an event.
files: src/store.rs: Store, call_from, set_state, reshape, commit, event
nodes.risk: State changes only here. Undo, events and attribution all hang off commit.

nodes.label: Verbs in QuickJS
nodes.what: A jelly's verbs are JavaScript. Each call gets a fresh engine: 1 second, 64 MB, no files, no network.
files: src/verbs.rs: run, check, eval, TIME_LIMIT, MEMORY_LIMIT
nodes.risk: Never give verbs network access. Live data is pushed in with `jelly call`.

nodes.label: Undo
nodes.what: Before a call, set or reshape, the old view, verbs and state are kept, 100 deep.
nodes.risk: Undo restores view, verbs and state only.

nodes.label: Attention and comments
nodes.what: Asks, looks and comment threads live on the jelly beside its state, not in it. Undo does not touch them.
files: src/store.rs: Attention, Comment, attend, answer, comment, reply

nodes.label: Headless Chrome
nodes.what: Whatever Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave is installed, run with --headless=new on /j/<id>/?agent=1.
nodes.risk: Shares one profile in the temp dir; it can linger after it is done.

nodes.label: jellies/<id>.json
nodes.what: One file per jelly: view, verbs, state, attention, comments and its undo history. Written whole, atomically.

nodes.label: events.jsonl
nodes.what: Every event, one JSON line each, append only. `jelly inbox` and `jelly see` read it.
nodes.risk: An event's `state` goes to live listeners only, never into this file.

nodes.label: assets/<id>/
nodes.what: Images, video, data beside a jelly. Outside state and undo.

steps.say: They click a button in a jelly's view.
The button's handler calls jelly.call("add", { title }). The view never writes state itself.
The runtime POSTs the verb and its args, signed by: "person", with the element they used.
The call route hands it on.
App::change takes the store lock. This lock is why verbs run one at a time.
call_from finds the jelly and gives the verb its state.
A fresh QuickJS engine runs the verb: at most 1 second and 64 MB, with no network. It returns the next state, or throws to refuse.

show.after:
$ jelly call plan add '{}'
jelly: title needed
show.caption: A verb that throws changes nothing; its message is the error.

steps.say: The old view, verbs and state are pushed for undo.
commit bumps the version and writes the whole jelly to disk.
The event is appended to events.jsonl: who, which verb, which args, which paths changed. State is attached only after this line is written.

show.after:
$ jelly call plan add '{"title":"second"}'
trial:plan v2: add ran · changed /items
show.caption: The CLI's one line is built from the same event.

steps.say: Back in App::change, the event goes on the broadcast channel, now with the new state.
Each open page's socket task forwards it.
The runtime keeps it if the version is newer, and calls every onState.
Every open view redraws: theirs, and anyone else's.

traces.title: An agent asks about one element

steps.say: It asks about one part of a jelly.

show.after: $ jelly ask plan "Which order?" --option a="Newest first" --option b="Oldest first" --at "#nope"

steps.say: The CLI turns the flags into one item: kind, title, options, anchor.selector.
POST /api/jellies/<id>/attention reaches attend.
The store lock, as for any write.
attend checks the item and gives it the next id: a1, a2, …
It is pushed onto the jelly's attention list. That list sits beside state, so undo never removes a question.
commit saves the jelly and logs an `attention` event.
The event is broadcast, so open views draw the card at once.
New in ef60c62. The ask has an anchor, so attend goes on to anchor_place.
It renders the page once, headless, and gives it 8 seconds.
In that page the runtime places the card, lists the open questions whose anchor matches nothing, and posts what is on screen.

show.caption: The card lands below its anchor, or at the top when nothing matches.

steps.say: put_screen keeps that snapshot in memory.
anchor_place answers as soon as a snapshot of this version is in, and drops the browser without waiting for it to exit.
The reply now says the anchor is missing, and placement turns it into a sentence.

show.before: asked a1 "Which order?"; it shows on the page below #nope
show.after: asked a1 "Which order?"; #nope matches nothing on the page, so it shows at the top
show.caption: Before, the reply named a place the card never went.

steps.say: It reads one line and knows to fix the selector, about 0.7 s after asking.

change.title: ef60c62: asks say so when their anchor matches nothing
change.note: Three places changed. The store, the log and the views are untouched: the item and its event are the same as before.
